skill.name: motion-graphics
skill.description: Creates short, design-led motion graphics such as kinetic type, charts, map highlights, webpage callouts, article cards, and logo stings.
skill.summary: Builds short, asset-aware HyperFrames motion graphics for social, product, editorial, and data stories.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The skill is functional but security-sensitive because it can execute local media tools, launch a browser, fetch remote content, and optionally use external AI APIs. Most markdown and template-literal hits are false positives, but the executable helpers and supply-chain behaviors require marketplace warnings and remediation.

remediation.issue: Initialization can update globally installed skills from GitHub.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before global updates, pin versions, and document exactly which repositories are fetched.

remediation.issue: Puppeteer runs with --no-sandbox while loading remote map and CDN content.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid --no-sandbox when possible, vendor required scripts locally, and restrict tile sources to trusted allowlisted domains.

remediation.issue: The locate auto path uploads user images to Gemini with an API key.
remediation.suggestion: Make remote upload opt-in per run, warn about media disclosure, and keep the grid-only path as the default.

remediation.issue: Helpers execute ffmpeg, ffprobe, base64, and ffmpeg encoding steps.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command names hardcoded, validate user-controlled paths, run in project-local directories, and fail closed on unexpected arguments.

remediation.issue: Localization docs and helpers use shared /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use project-local temporary directories or unique mkdtemp paths with restrictive permissions.

content.value_statement: Teams need polished motion graphics without building every animation from scratch. This skill plans, sources, builds, renders, and verifies short HyperFrames videos.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests into kinetic type, stat, chart, logo, lower-third, map, webpage, news, tweet, or asset-fusion categories.
Creates a shot plan with asset needs, layout choices, motion beats, palette, and export intent.
Uses HyperFrames catalog blocks and animation rules before hand-authoring custom gaps.
Can source or freeze project-local assets for search-driven webpage, news, tweet, map, and image workflows.
Builds renderable HTML compositions with paused GSAP timelines and deterministic HyperFrames metadata.
Renders and verifies MP4, WebM, or MOV outputs with HyperFrames lint and inspect commands.
limitations: It is intended for short unnarrated graphics, usually under ten seconds.
It does not handle live data at render time or live-action subject generation.
Search-driven categories depend on available providers, network access, and usable source assets.
Map and localization helpers require local tools such as Node, ffmpeg, Chrome, and HyperFrames.

use_cases.title: Social Editor Package
use_cases.description: Create short vertical graphics with kinetic type, article highlights, tweet cards, or lower-third overlays for fast publishing.

use_cases.title: Product Update Visual
use_cases.description: Turn a webpage, dashboard, logo, or feature screenshot into a concise animated product highlight.

use_cases.title: Data Story Moment
use_cases.description: Animate a stat, chart, map route, or geographic highlight as a clear visual beat.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Kinetic Title
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-second motion graphic with this headline: [headline]. Use kinetic typography, no narration, and render an MP4.

prompt_templates.title: Animated Stat
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an eight-second stat animation for [number] about [topic]. Include a count-up, one visual accent, and a clean final hold.

prompt_templates.title: Webpage Callout
prompt_templates.scenario: Search or capture driven webpage animation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this page: [URL]. Show a scroll, highlight [feature], add a cursor click, and export a short landscape video.

prompt_templates.title: Asset-Fusion Graphic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this image: [asset]. Fuse [data point] into the object geometry, locate the target accurately, and render a polished overlay.

output_examples.input: Create a short map animation connecting Paris and Berlin with a highlighted route.
output_examples.output: A brief map video with a frozen basemap, animated route line, city pins, labels, and a clean final frame.

output_examples.input: Turn this article headline into a social graphic with one keyword highlighted.
output_examples.output: A readable article-style animation where the headline enters, the chosen phrase receives a swept marker highlight, and the source remains visible.

output_examples.input: Make a product dashboard reveal with three KPI cards and one chart.
output_examples.output: A compact dashboard animation with staggered KPI cards, an animated chart panel, and a final hold for inspection.

best_practices: Provide the exact text, numbers, URL, image, or logo before asking for the render.
Keep one message per graphic so the animation stays clear and short.
Use project-local assets and verify the final render with lint and inspect.
anti_patterns: Do not request narrated, multi-scene, or long-form videos from this skill.
Do not rely on live remote data during render time.
Do not eyeball image coordinates when the locate protocol can ground them.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates short design-led motion graphics, including type, charts, maps, webpage callouts, article cards, overlays, and logo stings.

faq.question: Can it make narrated videos?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for unnarrated motion-first graphics, not long narrated videos or explainer scenes.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Some categories need network access for search, capture, maps, fonts, or external assets. Pure text and chart requests may not need it.

faq.question: What files does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces project files such as a shot plan, optional assets, a HyperFrames composition, and rendered video outputs.

faq.question: Can it create transparent overlays?
faq.answer: Yes. It can render overlay formats such as WebM or MOV when the request needs alpha output.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
